tasks.notes: Directly explains why verified bytes are not yet safe to expose and covers the cross-store, replacement, notification and collector claims, but it never enumerates the per-crash-window recovery evidence and records neither the pending operation, the nonpublic candidate identity nor the outbox event.

Explains the post-filter shortfall through the post-scan predicate order and candidate budget, the 40-candidate/two-eligible example, version-scoped mitigations and recall measurement, covering every core claim at least in substance.
Separates compensation from rollback and lists the five preserved obligations, covering four core claims fully and the pre-dispatch identity and unknown-outcome claim in substance.

Shows that the replacement keeps the same assignment slot so the overlap pattern survives, covering the s/N arithmetic, hash-independence and recovery-measurement claims while treating retry reachability and cell-based alternatives only in passing.

States the decision-relative omission test and the reviewable scope fields and validity ranges, but it never defines the model boundary as distinct from service or team boundaries and lists the recorded exclusions only generically.

Explains that the validator checks internal consistency rather than source correspondence and names verification theater, calibration laundering and evidence inflation, but it omits the unit and dimensional-analysis claim along with the orphan-model and stale-calibration-note cases and covers the verification-case rejection rule only partly.
